key_provisions: Amended the data center sales and use tax exemption; lowered the qualified data center threshold to $100 million; added a qualified large data center category requiring at least $2 billion of investment over 10 years; included electricity, water systems, storage, cooling, and related infrastructure.

sponsors: Rep. Aaron Pilkington; Sen. Jonathan Dismang
key_provisions: Created a sales and use tax exemption for qualified data centers, including data center equipment, eligible costs, services, and electricity; set the original $500 million investment threshold and compensation requirements.

sponsors: Rep. Rick McClure; Sen. Joshua Bryant
key_provisions: Created the Arkansas Data Centers Act of 2023 for digital asset mining; allowed digital asset mining in industrial-zoned areas not designated by the local government for other use; barred local requirements that treated mining businesses differently from data centers.

status: Died in Senate committee at Sine Die adjournment, 2025-05-05
key_provisions: Proposed to amend the Arkansas Data Centers Act of 2023 and regulate water-use and electric-grid impacts from blockchain networks and digital asset mining.

Created the Generating Arkansas Jobs Act of 2025; authorized strategic utility investment recovery and accelerated review of major utility facilities, including a six-month review period cited by state officials as supporting data center load growth.

sponsors: SB78: Sens. J. Bryant, Irvin; Rep. McClure. SB79: Sens. Irvin, J. Bryant; Rep. J. Moore
status: Enacted as Act 173 (SB78) and Act 174 (SB79), both act-dated 2024-05-03
key_provisions: Reworked crypto-mining regulation after local complaints; Association of Arkansas Counties reports Act 173 repealed limits on local noise and zoning controls, while Act 174 created an Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission permitting process for crypto mining.

sponsors: Sen. Bryan King; Rep. Ron McNair
status: All Senate resolutions (SR7-SR12) failed third-reading floor votes 2026-04-21 and formally died at Sine Die adjournment 2026-04-29; all House resolutions (HR1010-HR1015) died in House Rules Committee at Sine Die adjournment 2026-04-29. Underlying nonappropriation bills were never authorized for introduction.
key_provisions: Sought authorization to introduce nonappropriation bills on crypto-mining local control, extraordinary electricity-use fees, foreign hardware/software restrictions, money-transmitter licensing, six-month advance notice before land acquisition or construction, and water-use monitoring.
